node.label: Gary Gerstle
node.date_label: Working-Class Americanism (1989) · American Crucible (2001) · The Rise and Fall of the Neoliberal Order (2022)
node.description: Historian of American labour,political economy and national belonging. Gerstle’s concept of a political order explains how a dominant movement can require opponents to accept its basic terms. His account of neoliberalism links bipartisan political settlement to capitalism’s globalization and later crises,while leaving the form of a successor order open. Earlier work connects labour and nationalism rather than assuming patriotic language is inherently conservative.

incident_edges.relationship: Cites Gerstle’s examination of race and the liberal consensus when situating northern white workers’ resistance to civil-rights measures.

This bounded supporting reference is not formal mentoring, an exclusive framework or a claim that Gerstle authored all of Nelson’s analysis. Original Gerstle essay unread.
